name: Being a product owner
goal: So far, all projects have been collaborations with classmates, or there was only one stakeholder. In this project however, I have the full responsibility and need to make sure the project gets finished on my own.

approach.text:
In the design phase, there were many meetings with the managers, to make sure we were all on the same page. In the development phase, I had just a weekly meeting with the company mentor for a progress update. The planning was made very optimistic, as I planned to finish the base of the game within two weeks. I did not take setbacks or problems into account, and the company mentor quickly set me straight. He gave me an example of where he had to implement a feature, and an unexpected issue arised. If he had a very cramped planning, it would have been a big problem, but he managed to fix the issue because he added problem solving time to the planning.

Another important learning point was that I did not keep asking about things other people had to do for the project. The company had a model maker and a team of game designers. The models and textures were made by the model maker, and were requested rather late because of the planning. The team of game designers also made a texture, but for the overlay. The requests to create assets were made, but not checked upon, so I never knew if the people were working on them or not and how far they were. Luckily they were pretty quick and trustworthy, but I should have checked more.

normalLearnings: I know to include time for debugging / problem solving in the planning.
I know to check up on stakeholders more frequently to have a vision on the progress.
result: In future projects, I know to make a better planning and to check up on stakeholders more frequently. After the old planning was made and deemed unrealistic, I made a new one with more realistic time management.
validation: During the project, I remembered the old planning and reflected on them when I finished a task. It was clear that the old planning was made very optimistic. The company mentor asked me frequently if I knew the assets were worked on or not. Most of the time, it turned out that I did not know, so I took that knowledge for the future.
contribution: A more accurate planning as well as progress reports from others both contribute towards trust to the client / manager(s).
